literature_proposed.summary: A published theorem, not formalised. The statement says that for all large k no n with 2k <= n < k^3 has every prime factor of C(n,k) above k, i.e. g(k) > k^3 for all large k (2k > k+1 once k >= 2). Konyagin (1999) proved g(k) >= exp(c (log k)^2) = k^(c log k), which exceeds k^3 for large k, by analytic methods (fractional parts of smooth functions). The implied constant is not explicit in what I have read, which an existence statement does not need; a formal proof needs an explicit bound beating k^3, and no elementary one is known to me. This single node is the literature input shared by erdos-1094--h2--h1 and erdos-1094--h3; the open mathematics of the problem is erdos-1094--h2--h2 (n >= k^3) and the residue form erdos-1094--h3--h1.
